label: StudyE9b-dense Study 1 (StudyE9 re-run): OFFLINE REPLAY OF COMMITTED RESULTS (StudyD14b 0.25-s traces). CPU only on flash; no GPU, no model server, no inference. Scores are continuous log P(Yes); no literal Yes/No answer is used anywhere. Every score has a compute time and a delivery time = compute time + the MEASURED latency; the application reads the most recent score already delivered (sample-and-hold). AP is comparable WITHIN this grid only.
jpeg_note: (iii) JPEG upload, SENSITIVITY: model scores are the PNG scores; JPEG accuracy parity for S-EMBER was NOT established by StudyE10a-full, and Nexar ranking parity is cited from StudyE10a only.

b_zero_latency_delivered_equals_compute.description: Under setting (i) zero latency the sample-and-hold stream must equal the compute stream for every arm and every clip.

c_swap_resolver_to_4B.description: escalation-32B's code path run with 4B N1 resolver scores, 4B N1 thresholds and 4B N1 cloud latency must equal escalation-4B exactly (StudyE9's control).

d_shuffle_resolver_within_clip.description: resolver scores permuted across grid points within each clip (alarm FPR 5%, trigger 20%, cadence 0.5 s, primary config). AP must fall toward chance.

e_disable_delivery_link.description: CLAUDE.md Step 4: with L_cloud raised to 10 s (= L_max) no resolver answer can arrive before the episode caps, so escalation-32B must collapse to device-only.

decision_rule_1_capability_shortens_epis.statement: PRE-REGISTERED (StudyE9, unchanged): capability shortens episodes if escalation-32B has lower total cloud invocations per clip-hour than escalation-4B at matched tau_trig and matched alarm FPR, with a paired clip-bootstrap CI excluding 0, in at least 2 of the 3 alarm FPR levels, under latency setting (ii).

decision_rule_2_escalation_is_efficient.statement: PRE-REGISTERED (StudyE9, unchanged): escalation is efficient if it keeps AP within 0.01 of always-cloud at h <= 1 s (CIs overlapping) while using <= 50% of always-cloud's cloud work, at some tau_trig.
decision_rule_2_escalation_is_efficient.scale_note: On this grid chance AP is 0.00728 against 0.02806 on StudyE9's 1-s grid, so the unchanged 0.01 tolerance is 1.37x the entire chance rate. The rule is applied UNCHANGED as pre-registered; the scale-matched column is a LABELLED SECONDARY and is not the rule.

ap_curve_horizon_shift.note: CURVE SHIFT, NOT a per-event time: at the AP the 4B device arm reaches at horizon h, this is how much further ahead the 32B arm reaches the same AP, by linear interpolation of the AP-vs-horizon curve on the 0.25-s grid. It says nothing about when either model first notices a given crash.
